categories.label: V. God Names in Assiah
categories.description: The God-Names are the Hebrew divine names attributed to each Sephirah and path—words of power (e.g. Eheieh for Kether, Jah for Chokmah, YHVH Elohim for Binah) that name the specific aspect of deity governing that sphere. In ceremonial magic these names are vibrated to invoke the corresponding force; they encode, in the very letters and numbers of Hebrew, the theology of the Tree.

categories.label: VII. Orders of the Qliphoth
categories.description: The Qliphoth ('shells' or 'husks') are the unbalanced, demonic counterparts of the Sephiroth—the averse Tree of Death formed of the destructive residue of imbalanced force. Each Sephirah has its corresponding Qliphothic order, representing its shadow or excess. In the Qabalistic scheme they are not merely 'evil' but the broken vessels of an earlier, failed creation, and they map the perils and pathologies of the spiritual path.

categories.label: XIV. General Attribution of the Tarot
categories.description: This table gives the master correspondence between the 78 cards of the Tarot and the Tree of Life: the 22 trumps (Major Arcana) to the 22 paths/Hebrew letters, the 10 numbered cards of each suit to the 10 Sephiroth, and the 16 court cards to the elements and Sephiroth. It is the keystone that binds the Tarot to the entire Qabalistic system, making the deck a complete map of the cosmos.

categories.label: XV. King Scale Colors (Yod)
categories.description: The King Scale (attributed to Yod, the Father, in Atziluth) is the first and most spiritual of Crowley's four colour scales. These are the radiant, primary colours of the Sephiroth and paths as they exist in the highest, archetypal world—pure and brilliant. The four scales (King, Queen, Emperor/Prince, Empress) descend through the four Qabalistic worlds and the four letters of the Tetragrammaton, growing richer and more complex as they near the material plane; they are the basis of all colour magic, talisman design, and the 'flashing colours' used in ritual.

categories.label: XV. King Scale Colors (HEX)
categories.description: The King Scale (attributed to Yod, the Father, in Atziluth) is the first and most spiritual of Crowley's four colour scales. These are the radiant, primary colours of the Sephiroth and paths as they exist in the highest, archetypal world—pure and brilliant. The four scales (King, Queen, Emperor/Prince, Empress) descend through the four Qabalistic worlds and the four letters of the Tetragrammaton, growing richer and more complex as they near the material plane; they are the basis of all colour magic, talisman design, and the 'flashing colours' used in ritual.

categories.label: XVI. Queen Scale Colors (Heh)
categories.description: The Queen Scale (attributed to the first Heh, the Mother, in Briah) is the second colour scale, expressing the Sephiroth and paths in the creative world. Its tones are deeper and more saturated than the King Scale's, and it is the scale most often used for the Sephiroth themselves in Golden Dawn and Thelemic practice. Paired complementarily with the King Scale, it produces the vibrating 'flashing colours' employed to charge a symbol with magical force.

categories.label: XVI. Queen Scale Colors (HEX)

categories.label: XVII. Emperor Scale Colors (Vav)
categories.description: The Emperor (Prince) Scale (attributed to Vav, the Son, in Yetzirah) is the third colour scale, rendering the correspondences in the formative world. Its colours are typically blends of the King and Queen scales, intermediate in tone, expressing the paths most characteristically and used for the paths on a fully coloured Tree of Life.

categories.label: XVIII. Empress Scale Colors (Heh)
categories.description: The Empress Scale (attributed to the final Heh, the Daughter/Bride, in Assiah) is the fourth and lowest colour scale, showing the correspondences as they appear in the material world. Its colours are the most complex—often flecked, rayed, or shot through with other hues—reflecting the mixture and density of physical manifestation.

categories.label: XIX. Selection of Egyptian Gods
categories.description: This table attributes the gods of ancient Egypt to the Sephiroth and paths. The Egyptian pantheon held a special authority for Crowley and the Golden Dawn, who saw in its solar-and-resurrection theology the clearest expression of the magical formulae; the deities here (Ra, Isis, Osiris, Thoth, Horus, Nuit, and the rest) embody the cosmic forces of each station of the Tree.

categories.label: XXII. Small Selection of Hindu Deities
categories.description: This table attributes the deities of the Hindu pantheon to the Tree of Life. Drawing on the vast Vedic and Puranic tradition, it maps gods such as Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, and the Shaktis onto the Sephiroth and paths, allowing the practitioner to read the universal forces through an Indian rather than an Egyptian or Western lens and reflecting Crowley's conviction that all genuine traditions describe the same realities.

categories.label: XXXIII. Some Scandinavian Gods
categories.description: This table attributes the Norse gods to the Tree of Life—Odin, Thor, Freya, and the rest of the Aesir and Vanir mapped onto the Sephiroth and paths. The Northern pantheon supplies a heroic, fate-bound mythology (the World-Tree Yggdrasil, the coming Ragnarök) that resonates strongly with the Qabalistic Tree and the cycles of destruction and renewal.

categories.label: XXXIV. Some Greek Gods
categories.description: This table attributes the Olympian and other Greek deities to the Tree of Life—Zeus to the expansive sovereignty of Chesed/Jupiter, Ares to martial Geburah, Aphrodite to Venusian Netzach, and so on. The clarity and familiarity of Greek myth make this one of the most accessible pantheon columns for the Western student.

categories.label: XXXV. Some Roman Gods
categories.description: This table attributes the gods of Rome to the Tree of Life. Largely parallel to the Greek column (Jupiter for Zeus, Mars for Ares, Venus for Aphrodite), it preserves the distinct Roman emphases on law, state, and martial order, and supplies the planetary god-names (Sol, Luna, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) that underlie Western astrology.

categories.label: XXXVIII. Animals (Real & Imaginary)
categories.description: This table attributes animals, real and imaginary, to the stations of the Tree—the lion to the Sun, the eagle to Water/Scorpio, the unicorn and sphinx to their proper paths. Sacred and emblematic beasts encode the character of each force in living, instinctive form, and many double as the theriomorphic shapes of gods and as the kerubic powers of the elements.

categories.label: XXXIX. Plants (Real & Imaginary)
categories.description: This table attributes plants, real and imaginary, to the Tree—the rose and laurel to the Sun, the lotus to the higher Sephiroth, the deadly nightshade and the vine to their proper paths. Sacred herbs supply incenses, medicines, and emblems; their growth-habits, virtues, and traditional uses express the nature of each correspondence and furnish the materia of practical work.

categories.label: XL. Precious Stones
categories.description: This table attributes gemstones and minerals to each Sephirah and path. Stones have been used as talismans and as concentrations of planetary and elemental virtue since antiquity; here each is matched to the force it best embodies—diamond for the brilliance of Kether, ruby for martial Geburah, emerald for Venusian Netzach, topaz for the solar heart of Tiphareth. A practitioner may wear or consecrate the stone to attune to its corresponding power.

categories.label: XLI. Magical Weapons
categories.description: This table attributes the instruments of ceremonial magic to the Tree of Life—the four elemental weapons (Wand of Fire, Cup of Water, Dagger of Air, Pentacle of Earth) together with the lamp, sword, scourge, crown, and the rest. Each weapon is a physical embodiment of a specific magical faculty, consecrated and used to focus and direct the corresponding force in ritual.

categories.label: XLII. Perfumes
categories.description: This table attributes incenses and perfumes to the Tree of Life. Scent is among the most direct means of altering consciousness and of charging a space or operation with a particular force—olibanum (frankincense) for the Sun, myrrh for Binah and Saturn, musk and civet for the lunar and Venusian spheres. The right perfume attunes the magician and attracts the named power.

categories.label: XLIII. Vegetable Drugs
categories.description: This table attributes plant-derived drugs to the Tree of Life, reflecting the historical use of psychoactive and medicinal botanicals in mystical practice and Crowley's own pharmacological interests. (This is presented for scholarly and historical understanding of the system; it is not practical advice—several substances listed are potent, toxic, or controlled.)

categories.label: XLIV. Mineral Drugs
categories.description: This table attributes mineral and metallic substances used as drugs to the Tree of Life, a counterpart to the vegetable-drugs column rooted in the alchemical and early-pharmacological tradition. (Presented for historical and scholarly understanding only; many substances listed are toxic and are not safe to ingest.)

categories.label: XLV. Magical Powers [Western Mysticism]
categories.description: This table attributes the magical powers or 'siddhis' of the Western tradition to the Tree of Life—the specific occult abilities (e.g. the Vision of God, works of love, works of wrath, invisibility, divination) traditionally associated with each Sephirah and path. It functions as an index of attainments and of the operations proper to each sphere.

categories.label: LXXV. The Five Elements (Tatwas)
categories.description: The Tatwas are the five elemental symbols of Hindu (Samkhya/Tantric) philosophy used in the Golden Dawn as meditation and scrying devices: Tejas (red triangle, Fire), Apas (silver crescent, Water), Vayu (blue circle, Air), Prithivi (yellow square, Earth), and Akasha (black/indigo egg, Spirit). The practitioner gazes upon the coloured form to open the corresponding elemental plane.

categories.label: CLII. Perfumes (Ascendent)
categories.description: This table attributes incenses and perfumes to the Tree of Life. Scent is among the most direct means of altering consciousness and of charging a space or operation with a particular force—olibanum (frankincense) for the Sun, myrrh for Binah and Saturn, musk and civet for the lunar and Venusian spheres. The right perfume attunes the magician and attracts the named power.

categories.label: CLV. Goetic Demons of Decans by Day (Ascendant)
categories.description: These tables attribute the 72 demons of the Goetia (the Lesser Key of Solomon) to the decans—the 36 ten-degree divisions of the zodiac, taken by day and by night. Each spirit governs a specific decan and its planetary sub-ruler; the tables integrate the medieval grimoire tradition of constrained spirits with the astrological and Qabalistic frame, and supply the names, ranks, and seals used in evocation.
